text_zh: 吴宽，字原博，号匏庵（亦作匏翁），南直隶长洲（今江苏苏州）人。
text_en: Wu Kuan, courtesy name Yuanbo, art name Pao'an (also Paoweng), was from Changzhou, South Zhili (modern Suzhou, Jiangsu).

text_zh: 吴宽生于宣德十年（1435年），卒于弘治十七年七月十日（1504年8月19日），享年七十岁。
text_en: Wu Kuan was born in 1435 and died on the 10th day of the 7th month of Hongzhi 17 (19 August 1504), aged 70 sui.

text_zh: 成化八年（1472年），吴宽中进士一甲第一名（状元），会试、殿试皆第一。
text_en: In 1472, Wu Kuan placed first in both the metropolitan and palace examinations, becoming zhuangyuan (top jinshi).

text_zh: 吴宽中状元后授翰林院修撰，历任右春坊右谕德、左春坊左庶子兼翰林院侍读学士等职。
text_en: After achieving zhuangyuan, Wu Kuan was appointed Compiler in the Hanlin Academy and held various posts in the Crown Prince's instructional establishment.

text_zh: 弘治八年（1495年）吴宽任吏部右侍郎，弘治十六年（1503年）升礼部尚书。
text_en: Wu Kuan became Vice Minister of Personnel (Right) in 1495 and Minister of Rites in 1503.

text_zh: 吴宽虽为成化、弘治间最具声望的词臣，但终身未能入阁。据《明史》记载，阁臣刘健曾阻其入阁。
text_en: Despite being the most prestigious literary attendant official of his era, Wu Kuan never attained Grand Secretary status. Ming History records that Grand Secretary Liu Jian blocked his entry.

text_zh: 吴宽著有《匏翁家藏集》，原七十卷，子吴奭增补至七十七卷，收入《四库全书》。
text_en: Wu Kuan authored the Collected Works of Paoweng, originally 70 juan, expanded by his son Wu Shi to 77 juan and incorporated into the Siku Quanshu.

text_zh: 吴宽在成化、弘治间诗坛地位仅次于李东阳，其诗风自然天成、了无痕迹。
text_en: Wu Kuan was regarded as the most important poetic figure of the Chenghua-Hongzhi era after Li Dongyang; his poetry was praised for its natural, unforced quality.

text_zh: 吴宽书法以苏轼为宗，擅长楷、行、草书，尤精狂草，风格端庄严朴、浑厚凝重。
text_en: Wu Kuan modeled his calligraphy on Su Shi, excelling in regular, running, and cursive scripts — especially wild cursive — producing a dignified, weighty style.

text_zh: 吴宽在书法史上被视为吴门书派的奠基人物之一，其风格影响了祝允明与文徵明。
text_en: In the history of calligraphy, Wu Kuan is regarded as one of the foundational figures of the Wu School of Calligraphy, influencing Zhu Yunming and Wen Zhengming.

text_zh: 吴宽传世书迹包括《种竹诗卷》与《题赵孟頫重江迭嶂图诗》，被视为精品。
text_en: Wu Kuan's transmitted calligraphic works include the Zhongzhu shijuan handscroll and his colophon on Zhao Mengfu's Chongjiang diezhang tu, both regarded as fine examples.

text_zh: 吴宽与沈周为挚友。沈周曾为吴宽父亲庄园作《东庄图册》。吴人谚云：“吴人屈指先哲名贤，缙绅首称匏翁，布衣首推白石翁。”
text_en: Wu Kuan and Shen Zhou were close friends. Shen Zhou painted the Dongzhuang Album depicting Wu Kuan's father's estate. A Suzhou saying ranked Paoweng first among officials and Baishiweng (Shen Zhou) first among commoners.

text_zh: 文徵明为吴宽的学生。在尧峰山敬贤祠中，文徵明被列为吴宽的配祀。
text_en: Wen Zhengming was Wu Kuan's student. At the Jingxian Shrine on Yaofeng Mountain, Wen was enshrined as Wu Kuan's accompanying dedicatee (peisi).

text_zh: 王鏊与吴宽同为苏州人、同朝为官，曾为吴宽撰写神道碑，收入《震泽集》卷二十二。
text_en: Wang Ao, a fellow Suzhou native and court colleague, composed Wu Kuan's spirit-way stele inscription, preserved in Zhenze ji vol. 22.

text_zh: 弘治十六年（1503年），吴宽与王鏊等五位苏州籍京官组成“五同会”，取同时、同乡、同朝、同志、同道之意。
text_en: In 1503, Wu Kuan joined Wang Ao and three other Suzhou-born officials to form the Five Commonalities Society (Wutong hui), named for their five shared bonds: same era, hometown, court, aspirations, and principles.

text_zh: 吴宽曾任《大明会典》与《历代通鉴纂要》副总裁。
text_en: Wu Kuan served as vice-president for the compilation of the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming and the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government digest.

text_zh: 吴宽曾任孝宗朱祐樘与武宗朱厚照的东宫讲官。
text_en: Wu Kuan served as tutor to two crown princes: the future Hongzhi Emperor (Zhu Youcheng) and the future Zhengde Emperor (Zhu Houzhao).

text_zh: 吴宽并非“吴中四才子”之一。吴中四才子通常指唐寅、祝允明、文徵明、徐祯卿。
text_en: Wu Kuan was NOT one of the Four Talents of Wu. The canonical Four Talents are Tang Yin, Zhu Yunming, Wen Zhengming, and Xu Zhenqing. Wu Kuan belonged to an earlier generation and was Wen Zhengming's teacher.
